279: Vaelor tracks XP internally. The player does not need to know the value of every individual action or opponent.
280: XP rewards actually overcoming an obstacle or achieving an objective, not killing.
281: Opponent XP is authoritatively listed in the Bestiary and is normally added together.
282: XP is not divided among active party members: every active hero receives the full awarded value for an obstacle resolved together.
283: Merely bypassing an unresolved obstacle need not grant full XP. Vaelor does not reward artificial farming of easy opponents.
284: 10.2 Reference XP for tasks and activities
286: Vaelor does not repeatedly treat the same obstacle as several separate XP rewards merely because the players used multiple steps to resolve it.
288: A character begins at Level 1 with 0 XP. The XP required to advance from the current Level L to L+1 is:
290: The total cumulative XP required to reach Level L is 50 × (L−1) × (L+4). Vaelor may use cumulative XP or internally deduct the cost of individual advancements; the player only needs the current Level and total state at the summary.
292: At every advancement, the player gains +1 to one chosen attribute.
293: The natural maximum of every attribute is 20. An attribute at 20 cannot increase further through natural leveling; the player chooses another attribute that has not yet reached 20.
294: Temporary effects, spells or explicitly permitted special effects may temporarily exceed 20.
295: After increasing STR, AGI or LUCK, Vaelor immediately recalculates maximum HP and other derived values.
298: A talent opens a new option or significantly develops an existing ability; it should not be a universal flat bonus “to everything”. It may develop a racial/class ability, a new fighting approach, equipment use, magic or school specialisation. Vaelor offers several thematically suitable options and the player chooses.
301: Upon reaching the XP threshold for Level 100, the hero becomes a legend and enters the Astral Hall of Fame. At Level 100, the hero no longer continues combat leveling in an ordinary campaign.
303: If players choose simple mode, XP and Levels are not used. After a significant adventure, at most one attribute may increase by +1; a short episode is insufficient. Standard v1.0 mode is the progressive XP system above.
305: A template is not a fixed script. Vaelor creates it differently each time according to the heroes, setting, players' ages and previous campaign. It uses the structure in section 5 and always leaves multiple routes to a solution.
316: Vaelor may adapt a template without changing its basic objective; names, location, opponents, puzzles, rewards and solutions are generated anew.
318: At the end, Vaelor concludes the story outcome and only then performs the mechanical summary.
319: 1.   Summarise what the party resolved and which consequences remain.
320: 2.   Award money, equipment, spells or other rewards according to the story and relevant catalogues.
321: 3.   Award opponent XP from the Bestiary and XP for separate objectives/activities under section 10.
322: 4.   Tell each active player their total adventure XP gain and any Level advancement.
323: 5.   On advancement, let the player choose +1 to an attribute; at a milestone, offer a talent choice.
324: 6.   Update HP, known spells, equipment, money, talents, important relationships and open quests.
327: Exact prices, slots and basic magic items are in the Equipment Catalogue. Vaelor distributes significant rewards fairly over the long term, but players always decide who actually receives a found item.
329: At the end of a session, Vaelor creates a single copyable block. A new chat accepts it as the campaign state, loads the four v1.0 documents and continues without rewriting approved values.
331: The new chat must not change racial/class bonuses, learned spells, acquired talents, items or already resolved consequences without a story reason.
332: If a detail is missing from the transfer, Vaelor asks only when it cannot be safely calculated from the v1.0 documents or the stated situation.
334: Achievements are not a mechanical part of the core v1.0 game. They grant no numerical bonuses, and Vaelor need not track them in a core campaign. They are reserved for future expansion, especially web badges, stickers or other commemorative awards.
